sentence: This project studies how saltwater affects frogs and toads living in coastal habitats at different life stages.
This project builds a computational platform that helps design drugs made from living bacteria in the gut microbiome.
This project builds a microscope that tracks how proteins cluster and interact on the membranes of living cells.
This project builds a computer design tool for printing robotic materials that change shape, and studies how it helps girls learn.
This project studies how a retrotransposon inserts into the centromere of a plant chromosome and whether this affects cell division.
This project builds biosensors from engineered cells placed on lattices, borrowing ideas from solid-state physics.
This project automates an adaptive optics system on a telescope so it can quickly study transient astronomical events.
This project studies how fire and drought affect conifer trees and microbes, and how those effects change the forest ecosystem.
This project studies how bacteria use CRISPR to remember viruses called phages, especially temperate phages whose DNA enters the bacterial chromosome.
This project uses synthetic biology to make biosensors for contaminants in water, self-healing materials and gene therapy delivery mechanisms.
This project studies how speakers of different languages use words to talk about space, using experiments and computer models.
This project organizes a workshop on how science and technology can address water scarcity affecting agricultural production in arid environments.
This project uses theory and computer simulations to study how the protein shell of a virus forms and comes apart around its genetic material.
This project studies high-dimensional polytopes and how many faces they can have, using algebra, geometry and machine learning.
This project builds secure and easy ways to confirm who is using a device connected to the Internet of Things.
This project uses machine learning to predict how much product engineered yeasts make and to guide how those yeasts are designed.
This project makes porous materials called metal-organic frameworks that carry curcumin to prostate cancer cells, and tests how well they work.
